note: Hand-curated court orders, interstate disputes, and operational thresholds keyed to the Vaigai system. Sources are public news + court records; verify before quoting in print. Add new events here, then re-render the rivers page (no script run needed - the JSON is loaded directly).

events.title: Madras HC orders TN govt action plan on Vaigai pollution
events.summary: Justices G R Swaminathan and P Pugazhendhi took suo motu cognisance of dangerous pollution levels in the Vaigai. The court directed TNPCB and the state to file a report identifying pollution causes plus an action plan, and asked local bodies in Madurai, Theni, Dindigul, Sivagangai, and Ramanathapuram to submit timelines. Submissions in court flagged 177 sewage/industrial discharge points across 5 districts and 36 water samples below CPCB Class D (unfit for agriculture or industry). The Additional Advocate General admitted sewage mixing; an action plan was to be submitted by 20 Jan 2025.

events.title: Supreme Court permits 142 ft Mullaperiyar storage
events.summary: A 5-judge Constitution Bench held the Mullaperiyar Dam safe and allowed Tamil Nadu to raise the water level to 142 ft, struck down Kerala's Irrigation & Water Conservation Act 2006 (which had capped storage at 136 ft), and constituted a permanent Supervisory Committee. The 1886 Periyar Lake Lease Deed (999-year lease) remains the legal basis for TN's diversion of Periyar water through the Mullaperiyar tunnel into the Vaigai catchment - roughly 80% of Vaigai's annual flow.

events.title: SC Supervisory Committee remains active on Mullaperiyar safety + storage
events.summary: The Supervisory Committee created by the 2014 verdict still arbitrates seasonal storage decisions and dam-safety reviews. Kerala has petitioned the SC for the 2014 judgment to be reconsidered by a larger bench. Centre approved a Mullaperiyar safety inspection in 2024. Storage decisions here matter to Madurai because they fix the Vaigai's annual yield - a strict 142 ft cap during heavy SW monsoon means downstream Theni/Madurai see lower headwater + higher reliance on the (unbacked) Periyar dam capacity for direct release.

events.title: Vaigai dam release ~ 6,000 cusecs - Madurai flood warning
events.summary: Madurai city's Vaigai banks (Sellur, Anna Nagar, Anna Bus Stand area, Albert Victor Bridge, Kuruvikaran Salai) flood when Vaigai dam release approaches 6,000 cusecs. Lower thresholds (3,000-4,000 cusecs) saturate the Andipatti command area and trigger evacuation alerts in Theni first. The 2018 Vaigai floods peaked above 12,000 cusecs.

events.title: Vaigai listed as Priority III polluted stretch
events.summary: The Madurai-Manamadurai stretch is on CPCB's National Water Quality Monitoring Programme Priority III polluted list. Two NWMP stations - Vaigai U/S Madurai (10059) and D/S Madurai (10060) - track BOD, DO, conductivity, and fecal coliform annually. Latest readings show BOD jumping +1.2 mg/L through the city as the river receives sewage outfalls and textile-dyeing effluent.
